title: Python foundations
targetPerformance: After 20 hours, implement and explain four of five unseen small Python functions in 30 minutes, passing edge-case tests for syntax, strings, collections, loops, functions, recursion, exceptions, and simple classes; complete the reading-list build and text-analysis boss.
whyItMatters: A dependable Python foundation lets you turn a problem into a testable program instead of memorizing isolated syntax.

subskills.title: Read syntax and types
subskills.why: Names, literals, operators, and booleans are the vocabulary every later function uses.
subskills.selfCorrection: Read each expression left to right and check the value and type after every operator.
drills: Predict the type of a literal.
Trace a boolean expression.
Write a small predicate and test zero and negative inputs.

subskills.title: Transform strings
subskills.why: Text cleanup is a frequent boundary between messy input and reliable code.
subskills.selfCorrection: Test empty text, repeated whitespace, mixed case, and punctuation before trusting a transformation.
drills: Normalize names and whitespace.
Count characters by a rule.
Compare strip, split, join, lower, and casefold.

subskills.title: Use lists, sets, and dictionaries
subskills.why: Choosing the right collection makes membership, counting, and ordered data straightforward.
subskills.selfCorrection: Name the invariant: order, uniqueness, key lookup, or mutation; then pick the collection that provides it.
drills: Count normalized words in a dictionary.
Rotate a list without mutating the input.
Use a set to detect a repeated value.

subskills.title: Loop and build collections
subskills.why: Explicit loops and comprehensions turn a sequence of examples into a reusable rule.
subskills.selfCorrection: Trace one item through the loop, including the empty and boundary cases.
drills: Filter and sum values.
Stop when a duplicate appears.
Group records by a derived key.

subskills.title: Compose functions and closures
subskills.why: Small functions give a program named pieces that can be tested independently and reused.
subskills.selfCorrection: State the input, output, and side effects before writing the body; then test two independent calls.
drills: Pass a function as an argument.
Write a default argument that starts state.
Build a closure with private state.

subskills.title: Use a recursive base case
subskills.why: Recursion makes nested data and self-similar problems easier to express when the base case is explicit.
subskills.selfCorrection: Point to the base case and show how each call moves closer to it.
drills: Reverse a string recursively.
Sum nested lists and tuples.
Test depth zero, one, and several levels.

subskills.title: Handle expected failures
subskills.why: Clear exception boundaries turn invalid input into a useful contract instead of a mysterious crash.
subskills.selfCorrection: Catch only the failure the function promises to handle; let unrelated errors remain visible.
drills: Parse valid and blank fields.
Raise a useful ValueError for bad input.
Return a sentinel for one documented exceptional case.

subskills.title: Model small objects
subskills.why: A compact class can keep state and enforce an invariant when a handful of functions is no longer enough.
subskills.selfCorrection: Write the invariant in one sentence and check it after construction and every mutating method.
drills: Implement a value object with derived methods.
Reject invalid state transitions.
Combine a class with helper functions in a small project.

resources.title: The Python tutorial
resources.why: Use the official guided path for syntax, control flow, data structures, and functions.

resources.title: Built-in functions
resources.why: Check the exact behavior of common tools such as len, sum, sorted, and isinstance.

resources.title: Classes
resources.why: Review instances, methods, inheritance, and class design after the function drills.

barriers.barrier: Syntax lookup interrupts the first attempt
barriers.fix: Write a tiny example from memory, run it, and look up only the error that remains.
Add an empty input, a one-item input, and one invalid input before calling a function finished.

barriers.barrier: A failing test feels like lost progress
barriers.fix: Record the failing example and one lesson, then make the smallest repair and rerun it.
